profile_text.body:
OpusClip is an AI video clipping and editing tool, according to its website. The company says it turns long videos into short clips and publishes them to social platforms in one click, and that it serves more than 10 million creators. It was founded in 2022 and is headquartered in Palo Alto.

The site describes two models. ClipAnything is presented as an AI clipping model that works across genres including vlogs, gaming, sports, interviews, and explainer videos, rather than only video podcasts, and it accepts natural language prompts to select a specific moment. A separate AI reframe model resizes video for different platforms and keeps moving subjects centered using AI object tracking, with manual tracking available for more control. The company says the tool analyzes video content against social and marketing trends from major platforms, selects highlight moments, and assembles them with captions, AI-relayout, and transitions ending in a call to action. The site quotes Jason Lemkin saying OpusClip can do something he does not have time to do.

The company's tracked product is listed under video generation and editing, with video repurposing as its noted function. No lawsuits or MCP servers are recorded for it.
